Subject: Post-call: CloudHarbor integration checklist & model routing policy proposal

Hi Ethan / Maya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on the customer-facing assistant and the two-tier routing requirement (live support + async summarization). Per our discussion, I captured the core integration items and proposed next steps below. I want to make sure we’re aligned before Camila and Dev start the technical kick-off.

Top-level asks we agreed on:
- Pilot scope: query-time assistant for customer support (English, US region), rejection fallback to a smaller local model for low-latency path, and nightly batch reranking for re-training signals.
- Success metrics: sub-200ms median generation for short queries, <1.5x cost overhead compared to your baseline during peak, and reranker precision lift >8%.

Action plan (owners & timeline):
1) SDK & Auth: Camila to share a minimal SDK quickstart and recommend auth (API key w/ scoped roles vs short-lived OAuth tokens). Target: sample call in your dev env by 2026-07-22.
2) Routing policy draft: Dev to propose latency/cost policy that implements a 3-tier fallback chain (hot model in us-east, warm quantized model, CPU fallback). Target: draft by 2026-07-20.
3) Structured output & tool-calling: We’ll prepare a sample structured schema for ticket creation (+ function call example) and a safe-parser pattern to avoid hallucinated tool outputs.
4) Embeddings & reranker: We'll share a recommended embedding dimensionality and a small evaluation harness for offline reranker testing.

Attachments: cloudharbor-mvp-arch-diagram.png (high-level flow), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (ownership & dates), redwood-sla-draft.pdf (preview SLA).

Next meeting proposal: Wed 2026-07-22 10:00 PT for a 30-min technical sync to validate the SDK quickstart and walk the routing draft.

Please confirm the time and if any of the items above need to be reordered.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez

Sergio — thanks, this is helpful and aligns with how we see the pilot. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Auth: we prefer short-lived tokens generated from our identity provider (OIDC) rather than long-lived API keys for production. For an initial quickstart, scoped API keys are fine but we’ll expect the OIDC flow before production.

2) Region routing: US-only for the pilot. For the long term we’ll need EU region support for GDPR customers — we can scope that for phase 2.

3) Reranker signals: we have historical conversation data but it’s partially labeled. Would appreciate a small evaluation harness to validate embedding dimensionality and candidate set size.

We can do the 7/22 10:00 PT sync — Camila / Dev, please confirm if that works for you.

Folks — adding the initial routing policy sketch (summary here, full doc in Drive):

Routing tiers (pilot - US):
1) Hot model: redwood-gpt-13b-hot (GPU, us-east-1) — low-latency path for interactive chat (SLO: median <200ms for <128 tokens)
2) Warm quantized: redwood-gpt-13b-q4_0 (GPU/FP16 quantized) — fallback when hot capacity is constrained (SLO: median <400ms)
3) CPU fallback: redwood-compact-3b (CPU instance, small context) — last-resort to avoid errors, used for background summarization or low-cost queries (SLO: <1s).

Policy rules:
- Prefer hot until tail latency >95th percentile threshold or queue depth > 50 requests.
- Automatic spillover to warm quantized if hot latency exceeds policy or if budget burn-rate > configured%.
- Region pinning: for pilot, inbound requests from CloudHarbor US customers will be routed to us-east. EU customers will be routed to a future eu-west pool (phase 2).
- Reranker path: initial generation on hot/warm, candidate set sent to local reranker service (embedding fetch + cross-encoder) for ranking; batch rerank runs nightly to produce training signals.

Open items for Wed: exact thresholds for queue depth and budget-based spillover; quantization profile for warm model; and prom/trace hooks you want in the SDK.

I’ll bring a 1-slide policy diagram to the sync and a longer doc in Drive for tuning knobs.

-Dev
